amazon_listing.description: Read an Amazon product or seller page as data: title, price, stock, rating, reviews, images and specifications. Paste any Amazon product or seller link and Scrapeless reads the right kind of page.
amazon_listing.name: amazon_listing

parameters.description: The product or seller page to read, from any Amazon site.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: A postcode or ZIP code to price the products for. Amazon shows different prices, stock and delivery dates by address.
parameters.name: delivery_postcode

kind.description: Whether it was a product or a seller page.

listing.description: Everything Amazon shows on that page, as data.

ask_ai.description: Ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Grok, Microsoft Copilot, Google AI Mode or Google AI Overview a question and get back the answer they would give a real person, with the sources they cited. Use it to watch what the assistants say about a brand, a product or a competitor.

mock_response.answer: Several tools stand out, depending on...
mock_response.prompt: What is the best tool for web scraping?

ask_ai.name: ask_ai

parameters.description: Which assistant should answer.
parameters.name: assistant

parameters.description: What to ask, exactly as a person would type it.
parameters.name: prompt

parameters.description: The country to ask from. Assistants answer differently by market, so this changes what comes back.
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: Ask for an answer backed by a live web search. Only ChatGPT and Perplexity can be asked either way; the rest always search.
parameters.name: search_the_web

parameters.description: Bring back the products and merchant offers behind a shopping answer. Scrapeless charges twice as much for a reply that carries them. Applies to ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode and Google AI Overview.
parameters.name: include_products

full_answer.description: Everything the assistant returned, including follow-up suggestions and media.

products.description: The products recommended, when they were asked for.

fetch_page.description: Get a page exactly as the site sends it: the HTML source, or the raw JSON behind an address that answers with data. Use 'Read a page' when you want readable text instead.
fetch_page.name: fetch_page

parameters.description: The address to fetch.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: Load the page in a browser first, so anything the page draws for itself is in the source. Turn it off for an address that answers with data, which is quicker and cheaper.
parameters.display_name: Let the page run its scripts
parameters.name: run_javascript

parameters.description: Load the page from an address in this country. Use it when a site shows different prices, stock or news depending on where the reader is. Anywhere lets Scrapeless pick.
parameters.name: proxy_country

content.description: What the site sent back, unchanged.

javascript_ran.description: Whether the page was rendered in a browser.

get_account.description: See how much credit is left on the connected Scrapeless account and when the plan renews. Costs nothing to call, so it also makes a good first step for checking the connection still works.
get_account.name: get_account

extra_credits.description: Credit bought on top of the plan.

is_active.description: Whether the account is in good standing.

plan_credits.description: Credit left in this month's plan.

plan_renews_on.description: When the current plan period ends.

get_crawl.description: See how far a crawl has got and read the pages it has gathered so far. Check 'is_finished' to know whether more is still coming.
get_crawl.name: get_crawl

parameters.description: The crawl's id, as given back by 'Crawl a site'.
parameters.name: crawl_id

error.description: Why the crawl stopped, if it failed.

is_finished.description: True once the crawl has stopped running.

page_count.description: How many pages are in this response.

pages.description: The pages gathered so far, text and all.

pages_found.description: How many pages the crawl knows about.

pages_read.description: How many pages have been read.

status.description: Where the crawl is up to.

get_crawl_errors.description: See which pages a crawl could not read and why, and which ones the site's robots.txt told it to leave alone. Use it when a crawl came back smaller than expected.
get_crawl_errors.display_name: List the pages a crawl missed
get_crawl_errors.name: get_crawl_errors

parameters.description: The crawl's id, as given back by 'Crawl a site'.
parameters.name: crawl_id

blocked_by_robots.description: Addresses the site's robots.txt ruled out.

blocked_count.description: How many addresses robots.txt ruled out.

failed_pages.description: Each page that failed, with its address and reason.

read_page.description: Get a web page's text, even when the site blocks ordinary requests. Scrapeless loads the page in a real browser, solves any challenge in the way, and hands back clean readable text ready for the next step.
read_page.name: read_page

parameters.description: The address of the page to read.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: What each page should come back as. Readable text is Markdown with the navigation stripped out, which is what most steps want.
parameters.name: formats

parameters.description: Keep only the main body of each page. Turn this off when the part you need lives in a sidebar, a header or a footer.
parameters.name: main_content_only

parameters.description: Seconds to let the page finish loading before the text is taken. Raise it for a page that fills itself in after it opens.
parameters.name: wait_seconds

parameters.description: Load the page from an address in this country. Use it when a site shows different prices, stock or news depending on where the reader is. Anywhere lets Scrapeless pick.
parameters.name: proxy_country

description.description: The page's own one-line summary, where it has one.

error.description: What went wrong with this page, if anything did.

metadata.description: Everything else the page declared about itself.

raw_html.description: The page's HTML exactly as sent.

screenshot.description: A picture of the page, where one was asked for.

status_code.description: The HTTP status the site answered with.

text.description: The page's readable text, as Markdown.

url.description: The address the text came from.

read_pages.description: Read up to 25 pages in one step and get one entry back per page. Faster than reading them one at a time, and an address that turns out not to be a page is skipped rather than failing the run.
read_pages.name: read_pages

parameters.description: The pages to read, up to 25. Feed this the links from an earlier step.
parameters.name: urls

parameters.description: What each page should come back as. Readable text is Markdown with the navigation stripped out, which is what most steps want.
parameters.name: formats

parameters.description: Keep only the main body of each page. Turn this off when the part you need lives in a sidebar, a header or a footer.
parameters.name: main_content_only

parameters.description: Seconds to let the page finish loading before the text is taken. Raise it for a page that fills itself in after it opens.
parameters.name: wait_seconds

parameters.description: Load the page from an address in this country. Use it when a site shows different prices, stock or news depending on where the reader is. Anywhere lets Scrapeless pick.
parameters.name: proxy_country

pages.description: One entry per page, in the order asked for.

skipped_urls.description: Addresses Scrapeless could not treat as pages.

search_amazon.description: Search any Amazon site for products and get back the listings with their prices, ratings, review counts and links; the search page as data.
search_amazon.name: search_amazon

parameters.description: What to search Amazon for.
parameters.name: keywords

parameters.description: Which Amazon site to search.
parameters.name: site

parameters.description: Which page of results to fetch. 1 is the first page, 2 the next, and so on.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: A postcode or ZIP code to price the products for. Amazon shows different prices, stock and delivery dates by address.
parameters.name: delivery_postcode

products.description: The products found, each with its title, price, rating and link.

site.description: The Amazon site that was searched.

search_google.description: Search Google and get the results as data rather than a page: the web, news, images, videos, shopping, local places or patents, from any country and in any language.

results.snippet: This domain is for use in examples.
results.title: Example Domain

search_google.name: search_google

parameters.description: What to search for. Anything you would type into Google works, including site: and "quoted phrases".
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Which of Google's tabs to search.
parameters.name: search_in

parameters.description: Get the results someone in this country would see. Leave it empty and Google decides.
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: The language Google should answer in.
parameters.name: language

parameters.description: A town or city to search as if you were standing in it, such as Austin, Texas, United States. Worth setting for local places and shopping.
parameters.name: near

parameters.description: How many results one page should hold.
parameters.name: results_per_page

parameters.description: Which page of results to fetch. 1 is the first page, 2 the next, and so on.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Turn Google's SafeSearch on for this search.
parameters.name: hide_explicit_results

full_response.description: Everything Google returned, including answer boxes, knowledge panels and ads.

results.description: The results, best first, each with its position, title, address and snippet.

search_information.description: How many results Google has and how long it took.

start_crawl.description: Read a whole site by following its links, and get the text of every page. The crawl is not finished when this step is: it keeps running in the background, so follow this with a Wait step and 'Check a crawl'.
start_crawl.name: start_crawl

parameters.description: Where the crawl begins. Everything under this address is followed; start at a section to crawl only that section.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: The most pages to read. Each page costs credit, so start small and raise it once the results look right.
parameters.name: page_limit

parameters.description: Read only the pages whose address matches one of these patterns, such as blog/.* for everything under /blog/. Leave empty to read everything found.
parameters.name: include_paths

parameters.description: Leave out the pages whose address matches one of these patterns, such as tag/.* for tag listings.
parameters.name: exclude_paths

parameters.description: Follow links that point outside where the crawl started, such as a link from /docs/ to /pricing. Still stays on the same site.
parameters.name: follow_links_above_start

parameters.description: Let the crawl leave this site altogether. Use with a small page limit: the web has no edges.
parameters.name: follow_external_links

parameters.description: Seconds to wait between pages, to go easy on a small site. Leave at 0 to crawl at full speed.
parameters.name: pause_seconds

parameters.description: What each page should come back as. Readable text is Markdown with the navigation stripped out, which is what most steps want.
parameters.name: formats

parameters.description: Keep only the main body of each page. Turn this off when the part you need lives in a sidebar, a header or a footer.
parameters.name: main_content_only

parameters.description: Load the page from an address in this country. Use it when a site shows different prices, stock or news depending on where the reader is. Anywhere lets Scrapeless pick.
parameters.name: proxy_country

crawl_id.description: Pass this to 'Check a crawl' to read the pages.

page_limit.description: The most pages this crawl will read.

stop_crawl.description: Stop a crawl that is still running, so it reads no further pages and costs no more credit. The pages it already gathered stay readable with 'Check a crawl'.
stop_crawl.name: stop_crawl

parameters.description: The crawl's id, as given back by 'Crawl a site'.
parameters.name: crawl_id

status.description: What the crawl's state is now.

stopped.description: True once Scrapeless has accepted the stop.

description: Read web pages that block ordinary requests, crawl whole sites, and search Google (the web, news, images, videos, shopping, local places and patents), all as clean data. Look up Amazon products and sellers, and capture what ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Grok, Copilot and Google's AI answers say about anything you ask.
